title: Keep standards free of pipeline details
statement: Keep pipeline and data-format instructions out of a curriculum's descriptions, and don't remove a real constraint from a standard unless it is kept somewhere else.
detail: A procedure for reviewing edits to a curriculum data store, written from real reviews, sets as its goal never approving an edit that contradicts itself or strips a constraint without a replacement (`shadow/curriculum/.agents/skills/curriculum-pr-review/SKILL.md` line 10). Edits that strip internal field names and typing rules from standards are approved only after checking the repository's schemas: a typing rule that isn't in them was a leaked pipeline detail, and removing it is correct (lines 47 and 143). A removed rule is also fine when the standard's own examples already encode it (line 142).

evidence.quote: Goal: a deterministic, batchable review that lands quickly and never approves anything that contradicts itself or strips a constraint without a replacement.
If `stimulus_description` / `slope` typing rules don't appear in `schemas/*.schema.json`, they were leaked pipeline details and removal is correct.
**A removed rule is fine if the examples already encode it.**
